s.d: showing a high degree of refinement and the assurance that comes from wide social experience
x: his polished manner
maintained an urbane tone in his letters

s.d: Of a person (usually a man): having refined manners; courteous, polite, suave.
x: We took advantage of our acquaintance with the urbane Frenchman to join his party; the conversation turned almost entirely on literary subjects.

s.d: Of an act, expression, etc.: suited to a person of refined manners; elegant, sophisticated.
x: He [Yusuf I of Granada] had an excellent memory, well stored with science and erudition; he was of a lively genius, and accounted the best poet of his time, and his manners were gentle, affable, and urbane.
To guests, a servant should not sour-faced by, / But do the honours with a mind urbane.

the quality or character of life in a city or town

x: Arconum—I found two chairs wanting in the gentlemen's room, and the bath room attached applied to other purposes... the privies and urinaries clean...

s.d: of or relating to the function or production or secretion of urine
of or relating to the urinary system of the body
Of, relating to, occurring in, or affecting urine, its production, function, or excretion.
x: The objective is to make life easier for male colleagues and customers with urinary incontinence.

s.d: the system that includes all organs involved in reproduction and in the formation and voidance of urine
a membranous sac for temporary retention of urine

An elastic, muscular sac situated in the pelvic cavity, into which urine from the kidneys is temporarily stored prior to disposal by urination. Urine enters the bladder via the ureters and exits via the urethra.
a calculus formed in the kidney
difficulty in beginning the flow of urine; associated with prostate enlargement in men and with narrowing of the urethral opening in women; may be caused by emotional stress in either men or women
inability to control the flow of urine and involuntary urination
an ester with the chemical formula C8H7NO4S, produced in human body.
x: Urinary indican is produced in liver and excreted with urine.

s.d: an organ that separates waste substances from the blood and discharges them
holding urine in the urinary bladder
x: he has a problem with urinary retention

s.d: the system that includes all organs involved in reproduction and in the formation and voidance of urine
One of the eleven organ systems of humans, containing the kidneys which produce urine and the organs which remove urine from the body.
the organs and tubes involved in the production and excretion of urine
The continuous system involved in the production and excretion of urine; the kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder and urethra.
any infection of any of the organs of the urinary tract
An infection that affects part of the urinary tract.
x: The priest proceeds to pour bowl after bowl of ceremonial water on our scalps. My makeup, hair and contact lenses stream down my cheeks. My eyes burn. I wonder if I could get a urinary tract infection this way.

urinate.e: Borrowed from Medieval Latin urinātus, perfect passive participle of urinō (“urinate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), equivalent to urine + -ate. Compare French uriner.

s.d: pass after the manner of urine
x: The sick men urinated blood

s.d: eliminate urine
x: Again, the cat had made on the expensive rug

s.d: To pass urine from the body.
x: Our new puppy still urinates on the carpet, but we're housebreaking her.
Boys on their campsite should avoid urinating within 200 feet of the lake.

s.d: the discharge of urine
(uncountable) The process of passing urine, that is, of eliminating liquid waste from the body.

urinator.e: From urinate + -or (suffix forming an agent noun, indicating a person who does something).

s.d: a person who urinates
(obsolete) A diver, especially someone who searches for things underwater.

urine.e: From Middle English uryne, from Latin ūrīna (“urine”), from Proto-Indo-European *uh₁r-, zero grade of *woh₁-r̥ (“water, liquid, milk”). Related to *h₁ówHdʰr̥ (“udder”) (see udder). Cognate with Old English ūriġ (“wet, moist”). Displaced native English land (“urine”) (from Middle English land, from Old English hland (“urine”)), though lant survives with a specialized sense.

s.d: liquid excretory product
x: there was blood in his urine
the child had to make water

s.d: (uncountable) Liquid waste consisting of water, salts, and urea, which is made in the kidneys, stored in the bladder, then released through the urethra.
x: An artificial kidney these days still means a refrigerator-sized dialysis machine. Such devices mimic the way real kidneys cleanse blood and eject impurities and surplus water as urine.

s.d: (obsolete) To urinate.
x: He got out of bed every time he urined, or tried to urine.

s.d: any of the small tubules that are the excretory units of the vertebrate kidney

urn.e: From Middle English urne, from Old French urne, from Latin urna (“vessel”). Doublet of urna.

s.d: a large vase that usually has a pedestal or feet
a large pot for making coffee or tea
A vase with a footed base.
x: A rustic, digging in the ground by Padua, […]found an urn, or earthen pot, in which there was another urn.
His scattered limbs with my dead body burn, / And once more join us in the pious urn.

s.d: A metal vessel for serving tea or coffee.
A vessel for the ashes or cremains of a deceased person.
x:
So draw him home to those that mourn
⁠In vain; a favourable speed
⁠Ruffle thy mirror’d mast, and lead
Thro’ prosperous floods his holy urn.

s.d: (figuratively) Any place of burial; the grave.
x: Or lay these bones in an unworthy urn, / Tombless, with no remembrance over them.

s.d: (historical) A measure of capacity for liquids, containing about three gallons and a half, wine measure. It was half the amphora, and four times the congius.
A hollow body shaped like an urn, in which the spores of mosses are contained; a spore case; a theca.
To place in an urn.
an urn-shaped discomycete with a nearly black interior
having a concave shape like an urn
brown bile pigment formed from urobilinogens and found in feces and in small amounts in urine
(uncountable) A yellow linear tetrapyrrole resulting from the breakdown of heme, produced when urobilinogen is oxidized by intestinal bacteria.
a chromogen formed in the intestine from the breakdown of bilirubin; yields urobilins on oxidation; some is excreted in the feces and some is resorbed and excreted in bile or urine
(uncountable) A colourless product of bilirubin reduction, formed in the intestines by bacterial action
extravasation of urine into the scrotal sac
A swelling of the scrotum due to extravasation of urine into it.
passage of urine from the anus
passage of urine from the anus
primitive marine animal having a saclike unsegmented body and a urochord that is conspicuous in the larva
a notochord of a larval tunicate typically confined to the caudal region
A notochord that is limited to the caudal region; especially in the Urochordata
Any marine organism of the Urochordata.
primitive marine animal having a saclike unsegmented body and a urochord that is conspicuous in the larva
Any marine invertebrate of the subphylum Urochordata; the sea squirts.
amphibians that resemble lizards
Any caudate amphibian.
pain during urination

a urinary stone
A urinary stone, being any stone passed from the urinary tract, such as a bladder stone or a kidney stone.
a specialist in urology
A doctor of urology.
x: Dr. Schirren: The members of this round table keep on speaking about urologists and gynecologists but you never mention andrologists.

any pathology of the urinary tract

oil-secreting gland situated at the base of the tail in most birds
A secretory organ, at the base of a bird's tail, that secretes the oil used in preening.

uropygium.e: Mediaeval Latin, from Ancient Greek οὐροπύγιον (ouropúgion, “tail feathers”).

s.d: posterior part of a bird's body from which the tail feathers grow

ursine.e: Mid 16th century, from Latin ursīnus, adjectival form of ursus (“bear”) + -ine.

s.d: A bear.
of or relating to or similar to bears
Of, pertaining to, or characteristic of bears.
x: The British chief having undergone the ursine embrace of the Seikh monarch, the whole cavalcade proceeded towards the town.
[…] the old man's eccentricities, sometimes bordering on the ursine, repelled the juniors […]

s.d: Of, pertaining to, or characteristic of the bear subfamily Ursinae.
Covered in stiff bristles.
small ferocious carnivorous marsupial having a mostly black coat and long tail
any of various plants of the genus Ursinia grown for their yellow- or orange- or white-rayed flowers

urticaria.e: Borrowed from New Latin urtīcāria, from Latin urtīca (“nettle”) + -āria.

s.d: an itchy skin eruption characterized by weals with pale interiors and well-defined red margins; usually the result of an allergic response to insect bites or food or drugs
(uncountable) Itchy, swollen, red areas of the skin which can appear quickly in response to an allergen or other conditions.
x: "And the cramps when my body - like a badly articulated skeleton - would all get twisted into one rigid tangle! But now, except some dyspepsia and urticaria of the palms, I am free from pain."

urticate.e: From or formed like (post-Classical?) Latin urticatus, from Latin urtīca (“nettle”).

s.d: whip with or as with nettles
sting with or as with nettles and cause a stinging pain or sensation
To have or produce a stinging sensation, as of nettles or urticating hair.
Marked by the presence of wheals.
x: In certain cases of erythemata there was an urticate look.

s.d: an itchy skin eruption characterized by weals with pale interiors and well-defined red margins; usually the result of an allergic response to insect bites or food or drugs
a sensation of having been stung by nettles
(uncountable) The development of urticaria (hives).
(uncountable) Beating the skin with nettles (formerly used to treat paralysis).
x: The Romans had frequent recourse to urtication to arouse the sexual appetite.

urus.e: From Latin ūrus. Doublet of ure (“aurochs”).

s.d: large recently extinct long-horned European wild ox; considered one of the ancestors of domestic cattle
The aurochs.
x: He also brought forth two large drinking cups, made out of the horn of the urus, and hooped with silver.
